package_info.package_versions: Windows and Mac versions distributed prior to March 29, 2023 (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp package was compromised during the build process, resulting in the distribution of maliciously modified libraries (ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll). These libraries enabled the download and execution of infostealer and backdoor malware, allowing attackers to exfiltrate sensitive system and browsing data from customer environments without user consent.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when 3CXDesktopApp.exe is launched and loads d3dcompiler_47.dll)
execution_context.file_location: d3dcompiler_47.dll (maliciously modified, located in the 3CXDesktopApp installation directory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: RC4-encrypted shellcode is appended to the signature section of d3dcompiler_47.dll. At runtime, the shellcode is decrypted and executed, enabling the DLL to initiate network communication with attacker-controlled infrastructure.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code decrypts RC4-encrypted shellcode appended to d3dcompiler_47.dll, executes the shellcode in the context of the 3CXDesktopApp process, initiates outbound network connections to attacker-controlled servers, and prepares for downloading additional payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending encrypted shellcode to a signed DLL and executing it at runtime is a well-known malware evasion technique, allowing attackers to leverage trusted binaries to bypass security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs, especially those signed and distributed by vendors, should not contain or execute encrypted shellcode, nor initiate unauthorized network communications.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security or DRM solutions may use obfuscated code, but not in the form of encrypted shellcode appended to DLLs or for the purpose of unauthorized network activity.
key_indicators: RC4-encrypted shellcode appended to the digital signature section of d3dcompiler_47.dll
Execution of decrypted shellcode within the 3CXDesktopApp process
Unexpected outbound network connections initiated by d3dcompiler_47.dll

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when 3CXDesktopApp.exe is launched and loads ffmpeg.dll)
execution_context.file_location: ffmpeg.dll (maliciously modified, located in the 3CXDesktopApp installation directory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: A reference to d3dcompiler_47.dll is added to the import table of ffmpeg.dll. The modified ffmpeg.dll is designed to load d3dcompiler_47.dll and invoke its exported function, which triggers the decryption and execution of the embedded shellcode.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the modified ffmpeg.dll loads d3dcompiler_47.dll, calls its exported function to execute the embedded shellcode, which then initiates the next stage of the attack by establishing contact with attacker infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Altering a standard multimedia library to load and execute another DLL's shellcode is a recognized malware loader technique, used to chain execution and evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: ffmpeg.dll should only provide multimedia processing functionality and should not load unrelated DLLs or execute shellcode.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DLL chaining may occur in plugin architectures, but not for the purpose of executing encrypted payloads or initiating unauthorized network activity.
key_indicators: Unusual import or function call from ffmpeg.dll to d3dcompiler_47.dll
Behavior outside normal multimedia processing, such as DLL loading and shellcode execution
Modified import table or export functions in ffmpeg.dll

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after shellcode execution, upon successful C2 communication)
execution_context.file_location: memory (downloaded payloads such as ICONIC infostealer, guard64.dll, or Gopuram backdoor, loaded into the 3CXDesktopApp process memory)
required_permissions: network (to download payloads and exfiltrate data)
filesystem (to access system and browser data, and potentially drop files)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The shellcode downloads and executes additional payloads (e.g., ICONIC infostealer, guard64.dll, Gopuram backdoor) directly in memory. These payloads collect system information, browser history, and credentials, then upload the stolen data to attacker-controlled C2 servers.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the downloaded payload executes in memory, collects system and browser data (such as history, credentials, and environment variables), establishes outbound connections to C2 infrastructure, and exfiltrates the collected data to attacker-controlled servers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited collection and exfiltration of sensitive data, especially by a process not expected to perform such actions, is a hallmark of infostealer and backdoor malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not collect or transmit user or system data without explicit user consent, nor should it execute unsigned or unknown DLLs in memory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise monitoring tools may collect system data, but only with user consent and never exfiltrate it to untrusted or unknown infrastructure.
key_indicators: Network connections from 3CXDesktopApp process to known C2 domains or IPs
In-memory execution of unsigned or unknown DLLs (e.g., guard64.dll, Gopuram)
Collection and exfiltration of browser and system data by non-browser processes

attack_chain.action: User installs or updates 3CXDesktopApp, which loads the maliciously modified ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll from the application directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of embedded shellcode in d3dcompiler_47.dll

attack_chain.action: The shellcode embedded in d3dcompiler_47.dll is decrypted and executed, establishing contact with attacker-controlled command-and-control (C2) infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and in-memory execution of secondary payloads

attack_chain.action: Malicious payloads (such as ICONIC infostealer, guard64.dll, or Gopuram backdoor) are downloaded from the C2 server and executed in memory within the 3CXDesktopApp process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection and exfiltration of sensitive system and browser data

attack_chain.action: The executed payloads collect system and browser data and exfiltrate it to attacker-controlled servers, granting attackers access to sensitive information from compromised environments.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to exfiltrated data and can further exploit compromised systems

behavioral_signatures: Execution of RC4-decrypted shellcode from DLLs loaded by trusted applications (3CXDesktopApp.exe)
Unexpected network connections initiated by ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll
In-memory loading and execution of guard64.dll or Gopuram backdoor within the 3CXDesktopApp process
Collection and exfiltration of browser or system data by non-browser processes (such as 3CXDesktopApp.exe)
file_indicators: Modified ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll with appended or encrypted shellcode in the 3CXDesktopApp installation directory
Presence of guard64.dll or Gopuram backdoor in process memory of 3CXDesktopApp.exe
Unusual import or function references between ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll
network_indicators: Outbound connections from 3CXDesktopApp.exe or its loaded DLLs to known attacker-controlled C2 domains or IP addresses (as identified by threat intelligence feeds)
Unusual or unauthorized outbound traffic from 3CXDesktopApp.exe or its DLLs, especially to external or suspicious destinations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor 3CXDesktopApp processes for unexpected DLL loading and execution patterns, particularly involving ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll. Flag any RC4 or other encrypted data appended to DLLs in the application directory. Detect and alert on network connections from these processes to known malicious infrastructure. Use EDR/XDR solutions to correlate suspicious file, process, and network activity, and to identify in-memory execution of guard64.dll or Gopuram backdoor components. Implement file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized modifications to ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll.
